gloss: A fine needle on a syringe, passed through the skin into the lump to draw out a few cells. An instrument, not anatomy.
role: A fine needle can take a few cells from the lump. The result usually separates cancer from non-cancer, but it is not perfect: it misses some cancers and sometimes cannot give an answer.
matters: In fine-needle aspiration a thin needle is passed through the skin into the lump and a few cells are drawn out for a pathologist; ultrasound can guide it. A wider needle can take a small core of tissue instead (core needle biopsy).
